items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: Acute respiratory illness in PPDs and the CYPSE
items.summary: Managing acute respiratory illness (ARI) in prisons and other prescribed places of detention (PPDs) and in the Children and Young People Secure Estate (CYPSE).

items.title: Paediatric lung assessments: tips for practice nurses
items.summary: At a recent Nursing in Practice virtual event, consultant nurse and doctoral researcher specialising in respiratory medicine, Aleksandra Gawlik-Lipinski, offered advice and guidance on paediatric lung assessments.

items.title: Non-Invasive Ventilation Sleep Therapy CPAP and Sleep Monitoring Diagnostics
items.summary: SUPPLY CHAIN COORDINATION LIMITED. For the supply of devices for CPAP, Bilevel and High Flow therapy, their associated consumables, and accessories. Sleep Diagnostic and Sleep Monitoring Devices and all associated consumables and accessories.

items.title: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV): vaccination for older adults
items.summary: Information on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and the benefits of vaccination for adults and resources to promote the vaccination to older adults.

items.title: NHS Supply Chain awards National Respiratory Solutions Framework across 5 lots
items.summary: NHS Supply Chain has made award decisions on its new National Framework Agreement for Respiratory Solutions, covering respiratory therapy, anaesthesia and resuscitation, diagnostics and monitoring, nitrous oxide destruction, and respiratory support services.

items.title: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust — Neighbourhood COPD Risk Stratification Project - PCN Collaboration (C484015)
items.summary:

items.title: Respiratory Solutions
Benefits of walking outweigh air pollution risk for COPD patients
items.summary: People with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who live in areas with moderate to high air pollution can improve their long-term lung health with regular walking, a European study has found.

items.title: Vaping at home increases children’s asthma risk
items.summary: Children exposed to vaping at home are at increased risk of asthma flare-ups, according to new research.

items.title: PCRS webinar on breathlessness and chronic cough in adults, 30 September
items.summary: PCRS emailed members on 14 August 2026 announcing a webinar, Breathlessness and chronic cough in adults: challenges currently being faced by primary care, on Wednesday 30 September 2026, 19:00 to 20:00. Date and time taken from the PCRS mailing; not yet confirmed on the public PCRS events listing.

items.title: ResMed wins £9.8m, 5-year framework deal to supply Leeds Teaching Hospitals' non-invasive respiratory equipment
items.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust has awarded ResMed a single-supplier contract worth £9,798,912 (inc. VAT) to supply non-invasive ventilation and high-flow therapy devices, consumables and associated services for five years.

items.title: Trafford General performs UK's 100th Inspire sleep apnoea implant
items.summary: ENT surgeons at Trafford General Hospital (Manchester University NHS FT) carried out the 100th UK procedure for the Inspire hypoglossal nerve stimulation implant for moderate-to-severe OSA in CPAP-intolerant patients.

items.title: HRT ‘ups higher clot risk’ in legs or lungs regardless of dose or duration
items.summary: Current use of oral menopausal hormone therapy – better known as hormone replacement therapy (HRT) – is linked with an increased risk of blood clots in legs or lungs, a study has found.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.
